entities.summary: Charles III of Alençon was a French nobleman of the Capetian House of Valois. He was count of Alençon and Perche from 1346 until 1361, when he became a Dominican friar, and archbishop of Lyon from 1365 until his death.

entities.name: Charles III, Count of Alençon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Charles III, Count of Alençon, born on February 1, 1337, was a prominent French nobleman of the Capetian House of Valois, who made the extraordinary transition from secular lord to high-ranking cleric during the tumultuous Hundred Years' War. As the elder son of Charles II, Count of Alençon, and Maria de La Cerda, he inherited the counties of Alençon and Perche in 1346. His life trajectory offers a compelling case study of personal piety intersecting with dynastic obligation and political upheaval in 14th-century Western Europe, reflecting broader trends of religious fervor amidst societal instability.

From 1346 to 1361, Charles III governed his hereditary lands, participating in the complex feudal politics of France under King John II 'the Good'. However, in a move that significantly altered his dynastic path, he renounced his titles and secular life in 1361 to join the Dominican Order. This decision passed the countship of Alençon to his younger brother, Pierre II. His ecclesiastical career rapidly ascended; by 1365, he was elected Archbishop of Lyon, a crucial metropolitan see with significant spiritual and temporal influence in the Kingdom of France, a position he held until his death on July 13, 1375.

Charles III's renunciation of a powerful countship for the mendicant life and subsequent archiepiscopal office had lasting consequences for his family and the Church. His choice solidified the Alençon branch of the Valois dynasty under his brother, while his leadership in Lyon provided stability to a key ecclesiastical center during a period of ongoing Anglo-French conflict and the lingering effects of the Black Death. His life exemplifies the profound spiritual currents that could compel even high nobility to abandon worldly power for religious devotion, influencing the moral and administrative landscape of the French Church.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Charles III's unique life trajectory, transitioning from a powerful count to an archbishop, significantly impacted the succession of the County of Alençon and provided crucial ecclesiastical leadership in Lyon during a period of profound upheaval in France.
